images.title: Twelve millimetres is 1.2 cm
images.purpose: Show that 10 mm make 1 cm, so 12 mm is 1 cm and 2 tenths of a cm.
images.composition: A ruler strip across the middle with a bar above it; two short labels; white space around.
exact_structure: A horizontal ruler from 0 to 2 with big marks labelled 0 cm, 1 cm, 2 cm (3 big marks, 2 equal gaps), each gap split into 10 equal parts (9 small ticks per gap), grey (#6B7280).
Above the ruler a bar 12 small parts long starting at 0: the first 10 parts teal (#0072B2), the last 2 parts amber (#E69F00).
A bracket over the teal part labelled 1 cm = 10 mm. A bracket over the amber part labelled 2 mm = 0.2 cm.
Below the ruler, centred: 12 mm = 1.2 cm.
rejection: the bar is not 12 small parts, split 10 teal and 2 amber
the ruler gaps do not have 10 parts each
extra unit labels such as metres
any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: 10 mm make 1 cm, so each mm is a tenth of a cm.
images.description: A ruler from 0 to 2 cm with a bar of 12 millimetres split into one centimetre and two millimetres.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Count 10 parts for the first centimetre, then the 2 extra parts.

image_decisions.why: The bar shows millimetres turning into centimetres and tenths.
